title: Vivek and the End of Meritocracy
author: Travis Alexander
content:
![Vivek and the End of
Meritocracy](https://storage.ghost.io/c/65/af/65afbdb5-30bf-4286-acc4-9535069adb42/content/images/2026/11/54115700153_e7a96e5586.jpg)

For decades, the achievements of South Asian immigrants were celebrated across
the political spectrum as proof that the combination of liberalized
immigration policies and meritocracy could bolster the American imperium. No
one embodied this ideal better than Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican nominee
for Ohio governor. The son of Indian immigrants--an engineer and a
psychiatrist--he earned degrees from Harvard and Yale before co-founding a
biotech startup. Ramaswamy was well-positioned to demonstrate that America's
greatness lay in its recruitment of global talent. His 2024 presidential
campaign attempted to leverage that proposition into politics.

His timing was bad. By the time he came on the scene, much of the GOP was
souring on the globalist consensus that previously had made the immigrant
entrepreneur one of its favorite advertisements. The more stridently Ramaswamy
defended the old paradigm, the more the immune system of the movement he had
embraced treated him like a foreign body.

> "His timing was bad."

Ramaswamy saw the shift coming and tried to get ahead of it. During his
presidential run, he called the H-1B system "a form of indentured servitude"
and promised to "gut" it, though his own company, Roivant, had used the
program twenty-nine times. His proposed replacement, however, was revealing:
"The lottery system needs to be replaced by actual meritocratic admission." He
wanted fewer H-1Bs, but more merit.
